title: Mario Woods becomes obsessed with pyramids after Ellsworth abduction
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Mario Woods becomes obsessed with pyramids after Ellsworth abduction, about 1977 at Ellsworth Air Force Base, South Dakota, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.
place_text: Ellsworth Air Force Base, South Dakota

tellings.quote: Mario Woods, uh, from the Ellsworth Air Force Base, uh, abduction experience, South Dakota, 1977.

guys made fun of me in the missile field cuz I'd sit at the dining room tables in the day room and I'd draw a pyramid. I'd put a weird top on it and little sparks coming out of it. Now, I call that an Atlantean pyramid.
tellings.difference: Told firsthand: he drew pyramids with odd tops and sparks, he calls them 'Atlantean', and other airmen mocked him for it.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Mario Woods becoming fixated on pyramids after the 1977 Ellsworth abduction; here Mario himself describes drawing them in the missile field day room.

as_told.title: Mario draws 'Atlantean' pyramids in the missile field after the abduction
as_told.place_text: Ellsworth AFB missile field, South Dakota, USA

plain: In 1977, at Ellsworth Air Force Base, a US military base in South Dakota, a group of airmen say they had an encounter they describe as an alien abduction. One of them is Mario Woods. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, names Woods as one of the people from that Ellsworth event. Woods tells the rest himself. He says that afterwards he kept drawing pyramids at the tables in the day room, each with a strange top and little sparks coming out of it. He now calls them Atlantean pyramids, after the legendary lost island of Atlantis. He says the other men working the missile field made fun of him for it. So the host places Woods at the event, and Woods gives the firsthand detail, which, if true, suggests the experience left images in his mind he could not shake.
